When it comes to the IELTS listening tests, you may find it tricky and you might feel it as challenging. Most of the time, you will find it challenging to keep up with the speed of the recording and also in a different accent. Moreover, in the test you hear the recording for once. It is not possible for you to rewind it again or go back to listening to the topic again. Actually, this is what exactly makes the listening test more difficult. This is also a major reason to commit mistakes in the IELTS listening tests. The following tips will be surely useful for you in resolving these common mistakes.

IELTS Listening – Common Mistakes and Tips to resolve them

The Casper Academy of Excellence is helping students to focus on all areas of IELTS test and will help in an overall improvement. Giving best IELTS coaching with individual attention had made Casper Academy as the best IELTS coaching centre in Kochi. Here we are discussing about certain topics that you must be aware of while attending the IELTS listening test.

    • Blindly Listening to the Audio – This is a common mistake done in IELTS listening tests. It is advisable to understand the context of the audio and the information you will get from the topic before you even start. This will be helpful for identifying the answers in a better and progressive manner.
    • Avoiding the use of your Prediction Skills – IELTS test’s a candidate listening capabilities and their core understanding related to the topic through answering questions. Without predictions you may find it difficult to find your response from the audio played in the IELTS listening test.
    • Making Spelling and Grammatical Mistakes –Spellings also matters in the IELTS Listening test. Any word spelled incorrectly will be marked wrong in the IELTS listening test. It is important to correct such mistakes. Reading novels and newspapers for correct English and listening to as many as podcasts as possible for understanding sentence formation.
    • Ignoring the given Instructions – The listening test always start with a set of instructions that the candidates have to follow. You must strictly follow the instructions.
    • Losing your Focus – Another common IELTS mistake is many candidates lose their focus when they are unable to find their answer. Thus you must understand that leaving one question won’t cost you much and so don’t panic.
